one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience – poor communication and extremely slow delivery.

I placed my order on 16 August. Unfortunately, they were selling items online that were not actually in stock, which meant we had to wait for the stock to arrive. At no point was I proactively informed that the items were unavailable or that there would be such a long delay.

After waiting more than a week, the delivery was finally booked with Big Post on 24 August, with an estimated delivery date of 1 September. However, Aramex did not even collect the parcel until 1 September.

The parcel finally arrived on 2 September — 17 days after I placed the order.

What makes this even more frustrating is that we have now already left the Central Coast and moved to Queensland for work. Because the delivery took so long, my family now has to receive the parcel for me and send it all the way to North Queensland again.

This wasn’t a large or bulky commercial kitchen order — I only purchased small knives and a few small kitchen tools. The shipping fee wasn’t cheap either, so I really did not expect a simple order from Penrith to the Central Coast to take 17 days.

If products are not in stock, this should be clearly stated on the website before customers place their orders. At the very least, customers should be contacted immediately and given the option to wait or cancel.

Very poor communication, extremely slow fulfilment and a lot of unnecessary inconvenience for the customer. Very disappointing and I would not order from this company again.

I am a regular customer at this BP service station as I live nearby, but unfortunately, after today’s experience, I will not be returning.

Today, I filled up my car and went inside to make the payment. At that moment, I realised that my phone had been reset and I had accidentally forgotten my bank card. I calmly explained the situation to the lady at the counter and asked if there was another way I could make the payment. I also asked whether I could provide my bank or card details through their system. She told me to call a friend and ask them to make the payment. Unfortunately, no one was available to help me.

Instead of trying to assist me or explain the available options, she immediately told me that she would call the police. I was standing there explaining the situation and genuinely trying to find a way to pay. Eventually, she contacted the manager and obtained the bank details, and I immediately completed the payment.

What upset me most was the way I was spoken to. When I asked why she was threatening to call the police while I was clearly trying to resolve the payment, she said, “I am doing my job. You don’t have a mind,” and again said that she was going to call the police because I was “screaming” at her. I did not appreciate being spoken to or treated this way.

The manner and tone in which she spoke to me also felt discriminatory and racially insensitive. I cannot say what her intention was, but as a customer, the way I was addressed made me feel uncomfortable, disrespected and singled out. There was no need for the conversation to become so hostile when I was genuinely trying to make the payment.

I then asked for the manager’s contact number so I could raise my concern. She told me to wait because she needed to serve another customer. I waited, and afterwards she simply told me to leave and said that if I wanted to speak to the manager, I could come back anytime.

I understand that staff need to follow payment and security procedures, but customers should still be treated with basic respect and professionalism. I have been a regular customer because I live nearby, but after this experience, I will not be returning. I hope management reviews what happened and takes this complaint seriously, particularly the way customers are spoken to and treated.

one_star_reviews.text:
As a long-time customer since the 357 days, it is disappointing to see how much the atmosphere has changed. What was once a welcoming, inclusive, and community-focused venue now feels noticeably less friendly and far more uncomfortable. A big part of that change, in my opinion, comes from certain staff attitudes and the inconsistency in how patrons are treated. I have also become increasingly concerned about what appears to be a growing number of intoxicated patrons inside the venue and whether customer safety and comfort remain a priority. The sense of community that made 357 special simply does not feel present anymore.

My final visit on Saturday's towel-free night was enough to convince me not to return. I was physically touched by a staff member while leaving the towel-free area, despite already being only a few steps away from exiting. Moments later, I observed another patron wearing a towel walk through the same area and directly past the same staff member without receiving the same treatment. When I questioned this inconsistency, the situation escalated, and I was told to leave. As I was exiting, I heard someone shout "Never come back," which perfectly summed up how unwelcome I felt. Whether I am banned or not is irrelevant, as I have already decided not to spend any more of my time or money here. This review is not about the towel rule itself; it is about inconsistent treatment, professionalism, and the decline of a venue that many loyal patrons once valued.

I sincerely hope this has only happened to us, and that no other person has to go through what we experience.

AVOID

We paid $450 for a consultation. During the consultation, we were told that I would be provided with a surgery referral and a fertility specialist referral within a week.

After nine days, we still had not received the referrals. We contacted the clinic and were advised that the doctor was busy for the next two weeks. We were also told that preparing the referral to the public hospital was time-consuming and extensive, and that we would need to pay an additional $100 for it.

We also received a quote for laparoscopic surgery that was approximately twice the quote we received from another doctor. We were told the wait for private surgery would be around three months, which did not provide the quicker access to surgery that we were seeking by considering the private system.

Overall, we were extremely disappointed with the experience, particularly after paying $450 for the initial consultation and expecting the agreed referrals to be provided. Based on our experience, we would not return or recommend this doctor.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience of Dr Latika Sadashiv’s Specific Issues Report was deeply disappointing. I felt the report was substantially weighted towards one parent, with the mother’s presentation generally described positively while the father’s evidence, motivations and personality were subjected to considerably more negative psychological interpretation.

What concerned me most was the extent to which conclusions about the father’s intentions and psychological functioning were drawn despite the report acknowledging limitations in the objective collateral information available.

I also felt the children’s expressed views were interpreted predominantly through the framework of “dysfunctional alignment”, with insufficient consideration given to alternative explanations.

The report contained observations that could reasonably have supported different interpretations, yet the ultimate conclusions were presented with considerable certainty. In my view, this raised serious concerns about balance, methodology and the distinction between established facts, allegations, observations and clinical opinion.

Based on my experience, I would have been very cautious about engaging Dr Sadashiv for a family-law assessment or family-related counselling where impartiality and balanced consideration of both sides had been particularly important.

one_star_reviews.text:
My son attended the centre for two years.
While the first year was okay, our experience during the second year became disappointing.
There were times when educators and management were supportive kind and friendly, which i do appreciate but unfortunately, the ongoing issues eventually outweighed the positives for us.

Communication was poor. Most days when I asked how my son’s day had been, I was simply told “he is all good.” I constantly had to ask basic questions about whether he had eaten, slept, or what he had done during the day. He would often come home hungry, very grumpy and tell me about incidents and complaints for other children that I had never been informed about. I didn’t see the learning progress I expected, and most importantly, he was no longer happy most of the days. He would come home without anything positive to say about his day.
Whenever I entered the room, it often felt chaotic, with little sense of calm or structure.
I was constantly seeing different educators in the room, without any communication or explanation about the changes.

I raised my concerns repeatedly and attended several meetings. I was ignored by the teachers, and given assurances from management that things would improve, but I continued to experience the same issues. I also personally felt that some educators and management showed closer relationships with certain families and children, which made me very uncomfortable.

What finally pushed me to lose confidence in this centre was an  incident involving an educator that I believe was handled completely inappropriately. I immediately sent an email to the management, yet once again I felt there was no urgency or proper follow-up.
Whenever I needed to speak with someone, they were rarely available by phone, my calls were not returned.

I am extremely disappointed and have made the decision to remove my child from the centre.
This is just my own personal experience.

As a mental health professional, she lacks the most basic professional ethics, objectivity, and empathy for her patients. If you are looking for a therapist who can provide professional, rational, and genuine support, please carefully consider and avoid this therapist.

For instance, when I discussed a stressful incident on a flight where a passenger yelled at me after I accidentally stepped on their foot, her advice was to "act like a lunatic" and tell them to step on both of my feet. Rather than offering constructive coping mechanisms, her suggestions were unhinged and unprofessional.
What is most alarming is her retaliatory conduct. When I felt uncomfortable with her approach and exercised my right to terminate therapy, she subsequently submitted biased and inaccurate statements to the insurer, asserting that my condition was entirely unrelated to my accepted workplace injury. This felt like a deliberate act of retaliation that completely distorted my real struggles and ongoing trauma.
A psychological practitioner should embody integrity, empathy, and objective care. Her actions demonstrate a severe breach of professional ethics. Please think twice before consulting this provider.

We checked into this room and found mould throughout multiple areas of the accommodation, including the curtains, soft furnishings, around the door frame and in the bathroom.
The bathroom was particularly concerning. There was visible moisture in the bathroom ceiling, as well as areas where mould had been painted over. This was clearly more than a minor cleaning issue.
We immediately raised the condition of the room with Dean and requested a refund because we were not comfortable staying in accommodation in this condition.
Dean dismissed our concerns, told me I was “overreacting” and said, “You are not getting a refund.” He then said that he had cleaned the mould.
Every photo attached to this review was taken AFTER Dean said he had cleaned the mould.
As the photos show, mould was still clearly visible on the curtains and other fabric, around the door frame and in other areas. The bathroom also had visible moisture in the ceiling and mould that had been painted over.
This wasn't a tiny spot of mould that had simply been missed during cleaning. It was present across multiple areas of the room and bathroom, including fabric furnishings.
We gave Dean the opportunity to resolve the situation by requesting a refund so we could leave and find somewhere else to stay. Instead, our concerns were dismissed, I was told I was overreacting, and we were flatly told we would not be getting a refund.
For anyone considering staying here, look closely at the attached photos and make your own judgement. These photos are the condition of the room AFTER Dean said he had cleaned the mould.
Based on both the condition of the accommodation and the way our complaint was handled, I would not recommend staying here.

one_star_reviews.text:
My son and I visited this op shop, and he found a Batman car set. I had already looked online to see if it was a complete set because all the pieces were priced separately and, when added together, came to around $20. The set was clearly second-hand and used and wasn’t even in the best condition.

I politely asked the lady at the counter how much the set would be if purchased together. Unfortunately, she was very dismissive of what I was asking and came across as extremely rude. She proceeded to tell me that “they need to make money, the same as me.”

I completely understand that op shops need to make money, but so do families. I’m a mum with a young child, and with the cost of living being what it is these days, I don’t appreciate seeing second-hand donated items being priced almost the same as what you would pay in other shops for new products.

It’s also the way I was spoken to that really disappointed me. There was no need to be rude or dismissive when I was simply asking a reasonable question about purchasing the set together.

We ended up going to another op shop afterwards, where my son found a massive bag containing a train set for only $6! That experience showed me that there are still op shops out there offering genuine bargains and treating customers kindly.

I understand that prices need to cover costs, but op shops should also remember the families and communities they are meant to support. Sadly, this experience left a very bad impression on me.

one_star_reviews.text:
These facilities really need to be reconsidered from an accessibility perspective.
As an AuDHD person, I found the accessible toilet a sensory nightmare. There is no normal toilet seat — you're expected to sit directly on a stainless-steel rim, which was extremely uncomfortable from a sensory perspective.
The layout is frustrating as well. To access the accessible toilet, you have to navigate around the door of the neighbouring toilet/cubicle. I've only personally used a wheelchair for around a month in the past, but that experience gave me a much better understanding of how frustrating unnecessarily complicated layouts like this can be. An accessible facility shouldn't require someone to manoeuvre around poorly positioned doors just to reach it.

The accessible shower area isn't much better. The bench provided is very small and there is virtually no privacy for someone who needs extra time or space to dry and get dressed. Realistically, someone needing privacy or assistance to change is likely to end up using the accessible toilet as a changing area instead, making that toilet unavailable to somebody who actually needs to use it.

I wasn’t expecting the Taj Mahal of toilets but accessibility is more than putting up a wheelchair symbol and installing grab rails. The whole facility needs to be usable in practice, including for people with mobility, sensory and privacy needs.

I cannot speak for the entire staff, as my experience was limited to a phone call with the receptionist, but unfortunately, that interaction was extremely disappointing and unprofessional.
I called simply to enquire about appointment availability for my mother and to find out whether there was another specialist who might be able to see her, rather than the specific doctor listed on her referral. Instead of receiving basic assistance or a professional response, I was met with an incredibly rude, dismissive and unnecessarily aggressive attitude.

The receptionist questioned how I had obtained the phone number, repeatedly asked for the name of the doctor, and insisted that they did not have these doctors and that she did not know the doctor I was referring to. This was completely beside the point of my enquiry. I was not demanding an appointment with that particular doctor; I was simply asking whether another specialist was available.

What should have been a straightforward conversation became an unnecessarily unpleasant experience because of the way I was spoken to. There was little willingness to listen to my actual question, clarify what I needed or offer any meaningful assistance.

For a medical practice, where patients and their families may already be dealing with stressful circumstances, this level of communication is simply unacceptable. A receptionist is often the first point of contact for a practice, and the way they speak to people reflects directly on the professionalism and reputation of the business.

I understand that reception staff can be busy, but that is no excuse for being rude, dismissive or confrontational towards someone making a perfectly reasonable enquiry. I called seeking information, not an argument.

Based on this interaction alone, I was left with a very poor impression of the practice. I sincerely hope management addresses how enquiries are handled, because no one should have to deal with this attitude simply for trying to arrange appropriate medical care for a family member.

I had a very disappointing experience with Law Works Compensation Lawyers, who wasted nearly five months of my time. Principal Solicitor Angelica Villar provided written advice stating my injury had not resulted in surgery. This was completely incorrect, as official hospital and reports supplied directly to her office explicitly detailed a surgical procedure to remove deep glass fragments from my heel. It left me severely skeptical of how a principal solicitor who overlooks primary medical details could effectively represent my matter for the best outcome.

Additionally, while describing my case as a "modest claim", her proposed Costs Agreement required contracting out of standard NSW statutory cost caps ($10,000 or 20% max fee cap), exposing me to higher percentage fees and $500/hr rates. When I pointed out these factual errors and questioned the fee structure, she dismissed my concerns, made baseless comments about how my email was written, and closed the file.

I cannot recommend this practice due to their lack of attention to primary medical evidence, long delays, and unreasonable fee structures.

Extremely disappointing and traumatic experience.

In March, my 3 year-old daughter had Rumi braids done at Braidz & Co. The braids were left in for approximately 24 hours, and unfortunately, the experience resulted in a severe scalp infection that she has continued  not to heal for the past 7 months.

She also suffered significant traction alopecia from the braids being excessively tight, leaving a large section across the top of her head completely bald. What should have been a fun experience for a little girl has instead resulted in ongoing medical treatment, distress and trauma. She is now under specialist care and requires plastic surgery at just 3 years old.

What has been most disappointing is the response from Braidz & Co. Throughout this ordeal, we have received no meaningful accountability or support. There has been no offer to assist with what has happened, no indication that staff will receive additional training, and no genuine acknowledgement of the seriousness of the situation.

This wasn’t simply a case of a hairstyle not turning out as expected. A 3-year-old has suffered a serious and ongoing scalp injury with consequences that may affect her for years to come.

As a parent, I trusted this business with my daughter’s care, and I deeply regret that decision. I would strongly encourage other parents to carefully consider the risks before having their young child’s hair braided here.

Only knowing a skill is not enough, you need to have people and social skill as well when running a business.

I am happy to pay more at some other place but with well behaved people, instead of ill mannered staff.

one_star_reviews.text: Warning, to new clients.  Expect a very poor, slow and inaccurate service from the Office staff..Expect to make 5 calls and contacts yet not get an appointment.  They make multiple mistakes,  no appointments made, no accurate charging rates on sheet, and Expect to Pay $800 for initial 40 min visit and $500 for each 40min appoints thereafter... they may state its $295 or $375 but its much more... The staff will debate which code to charge you under.... I wish I had read that the Majority ( nearly every client ) has had a very bad experience....

I very rarely leave negative reviews, particularly when it comes to healthcare, but my experience with Dr Ayeni and Perth Clinic was extremely disappointing.

During what was already a very difficult and vulnerable period for me, I was actively trying to ensure that all of the healthcare professionals involved in my treatment were communicating and working from the same information. My GP, nurse and counsellor were all involved and made genuine efforts to coordinate my care. Unfortunately, I did not feel that same level of engagement or professionalism from Dr Ayeni.

Communication was incredibly difficult from the beginning. Emails and attempts to clarify important aspects of my treatment seemed to go unanswered, getting assistance through reception was frustrating, and I repeatedly felt as though I was chasing basic communication that should not have been so difficult to obtain.

What concerned me most was feeling that my medical history, notes and the information being provided by the other professionals involved in my care had not been properly considered. Decisions and uncertainty surrounding medication I had been prescribed for many years caused me an enormous amount of unnecessary anxiety. My nurse ultimately felt strongly enough about the situation to seek independent clinical advice and write directly to Dr Ayeni outlining her concerns and advocating for a coordinated, gradual and clinically appropriate approach to my care.

I went into this process genuinely asking for help and trying to do everything correctly. Instead of feeling supported for being open and proactive about my health, I left appointments feeling unheard, anxious and, at times, as though I was being punished for asking for help.

Healthcare — particularly mental healthcare — requires communication, compassion and collaboration. When several professionals are trying to work together for a patient’s wellbeing, I don’t think it is unreasonable to expect a specialist to read the relevant information, communicate with the treating team and make the patient feel that they are part of their own treatment rather than an inconvenience.

Thankfully, I now have continuity of care elsewhere and will not need to return. Based on my personal experience, I could not recommend Dr Ayeni.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was initially very impressed with West Coast Neuro. Renae was absolutely lovely at our first meet and greet and came across as professional, understanding and knowledgeable. I had provided all relevant documentation beforehand, and she was fully aware of my son's history, including his TBI and significant psychosocial behaviours. I was specifically told that she had experience with TBIs and neuro related conditions.

Renae spent approximately an hour and a half with us at the initial appointment, for which I was charged close to $700, including additional time, travel and kilometres. I was happy to proceed because I believed I was paying for a Functional Capacity Assessment, or FCA, which was the service outlined in the paperwork I had signed.

During that first appointment, I became extremely overwhelmed and actually broke down in front of Renae. She could visibly see how stressed and distressed I was and was aware of how difficult things had been for our family. She also knew that our weekends were particularly turbulent and tumultuous.

Despite this, I heard very little from her afterwards. Almost four weeks after our initial meeting, around the time I was expecting the report, I was told that Renae was unable to support us. She then advised that she had contacted another organisation and was waiting for a response.

This was extremely disappointing. If there were concerns about whether she could complete the FCA, I believe this should have been identified and communicated from the beginning. She had all of the relevant information about my son's history from the beginning and had already met with us and seen firsthand how much we were struggling.

The lack of contact and communication during those almost four weeks was particularly disappointing given how much she knew about our circumstances. I feel that more proactive communication should have occurred rather than leaving us waiting for weeks, believing that the assessment was almost complete.

I subsequently contacted the business owner to request that some of the money be refunded, particularly as I had paid for an FCA and was ultimately told that the service could not be provided. I was also advised that essentially no work had been completed on my case, despite the substantial amount I had already paid. They wanted  to charge me for a handover basically sending my documents to the new OT.

The owner promised me a phone call on Friday regarding the matter. It has now been almost a week, and I am still waiting for that call.

Unfortunately, based on my experience, I would not recommend West Coast Neuro. My biggest issue is not that they were unable to assist. It is the lack of communication, the length of time it took to tell me they could not assist, and the fact that this occurred despite them being fully aware of my son's history and our circumstances from the very beginning.

I feel that a large sum of amount of money was spent for a service that ultimately was not delivered, and the lack of communication throughout the process made an already incredibly stressful situation even harder.

MY EXPERIENCE WITH THE PHONE SURGERY KIAMA – PLEASE READ BEFORE USING THEM
I recently had the screen replaced on my Samsung Z Fold 5, which is approximately two years old. I was initially quoted three different prices by The Phone Surgery, and I had to question why the prices kept changing.
I eventually agreed to pay $685 for what I was told was a new Samsung screen, with a 3-month warranty.
Unfortunately, just two weeks after the repair, lines appeared across the screen.
I contacted The Phone Surgery and was asked to come into the store two days later to speak with the owner. I made the 20 minute trip to the store, only to be told that the owner wasn't available. I waited approximately 40 minutes, but the owner still did not appear.
I then asked for the owner to contact me directly. I never received that call.
The most disappointing part of this experience was not simply that the screen developed a problem after only two weeks — it was how my warranty concern was handled afterwards.
I paid $685 for the repair and, based on my experience, I did not feel that my warranty concern was properly addressed.
This review is based entirely on my personal experience and what happened to me.
I strongly recommend that anyone considering an expensive phone repair gets the warranty terms in writing and understands exactly what is covered before handing over their money.
For me, unfortunately, this was a very disappointing experience and I would not use The Phone Surgery again.
Given that their own website says repairs carry a warranty.

one_star_reviews.text:
We visited Zilver Restaurant on Friday night as a group of three, and unfortunately the service was extremely disappointing from the moment we arrived.

There was nobody to greet us on arrival. We were pointed to a table near the entrance by the cashier, which we felt was poorly positioned as crowded area so we asked if we could sit at a better table across the room. We ended up walking over to the table ourselves, while the staff member muttered something in Chinese to her colleagues, seemingly in disagreement with our request. Not a great first impression.

Nobody offered us menus. An older gentleman who spoke very little English came over and gestured as though asking if we wanted beers. We asked for menus and he brought us one — for three people. We then had to flag down another waiter to ask for additional menus and eventually place our order.

The food itself arrived relatively quickly, but again the service was lacking. No soy sauce or chilli sauce was provided, so we had to ask. We were also only given chopsticks and had to ask for cutlery. We have no problem using chopsticks, but given the price point, basic cutlery should be provided without having to request it.

The food was reasonable, but certainly not impressive enough to justify the prices, which we found to be very expensive. I’d rate it 6.5/10

The atmosphere was also disappointing. It feels more like a convention hall than a restaurant, with very little ambience and virtually no warmth or hospitality from the staff. There were no smiles or welcoming interactions throughout our visit. At one point, the older gentleman who initially served us walked past pushing a green Coles trolley with plates on it — something I’ve never seen in a restaurant of this supposed standard.

Our bill came to $260 for three people. At that price, we expected a significantly higher level of food, service and overall experience.

Unfortunately, Zilver did not deliver. We won’t be returning.
Reservations not required

Very disappointing product and after-sales support.

I purchased a Pure Design XC-10 Climber for more than $2,500, and it had a fault from the time it arrived. It took repeated emails and follow-ups before a technician was finally sent to inspect it—nearly six weeks in total.

Within a year, another fault developed. The right pedal mechanism is no longer tracking correctly and is scraping against the metal frame. Once again, I have had to repeatedly chase support. It has now been over four weeks, and my last three emails have received no response.

For a piece of equipment costing more than $2,500, I expected far better reliability and significantly better after-sales service.

I have owned Concept2 rowers and SkiErgs and have never experienced reliability or support issues like this. Based on my experience, I would not recommend the Pure Design products to anyone.

I’m a big supporter of Wagga businesses and this is the first Google review I have left. Unfortunately, it follows the worst customer service experience I have ever had.

I left my damaged phone with SOS Phone Repairs Wagga in February and was told it would take approximately 2–3 weeks to attempt to recover my photos and data.

I got my phone back in August. Six months later.

In those six months, I did not receive a single phone call from the Wagga store. Every single update was initiated by me, either calling or going into the store. Each time I followed up, I seemed to receive a different explanation about where my phone was, what had happened and what was happening next.

It eventually reached the point where, after so many different stories, I told the store I no longer had confidence in what I was being told and was genuinely concerned they had lost my phone. I raised my concerns directly and asked for my phone to simply be returned.

Still, no one contacted me. I had to chase them again.

I was also extremely concerned to discover that the information being used to identify my phone between Wagga and the repairer in Melbourne was apparently just “iPhone 13”, without even my name attached.

In the end, the only reason I got my phone back was because I called the SOS number and was connected to the Coffs Harbour store. Their staff were fantastic. They took ownership of an issue that wasn't theirs, contacted Wagga on my behalf, kept me updated and had my phone returned within a week. The contrast in customer service was remarkable.

I completely understand that recovering my data may not have been possible. That isn't why I'm leaving this review.

Being quoted 2–3 weeks and then spending six months chasing the return of my own phone, without receiving a single proactive call from the Wagga store, even after making a complaint and raising concerns, is simply unacceptable.

I would not recommend SOS Phone Repairs Wagga.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was really looking forward to visiting this venue with my friends from Melbourne,

Unfortunately, the night quickly became uncomfortable. When we first arrived, a large middle aged  man verbally growled at us and deliberately adopted a threatening posture. Later, while my husband was returning from getting drinks, the same man pushed into him, causing the drinks to spill.

Throughout the night, this man continued behaving aggressively in the common area, repeatedly smashing glasses and yelling at people. We immediately brought this to the attention of security because we genuinely felt unsafe.

What was most disappointing was that, rather than making us feel protected, security appeared to defend the man’s behaviour and tried to reassure us that it was acceptable. From our perspective, it absolutely was not.

My friends and family ultimately decided to leave because we no longer felt safe staying. What should have been an enjoyable night celebrating my cousin’s engagement ended with us feeling extremely uncomfortable and disappointed.

I would not return to this venue and, based on our experience, I would be hesitant to recommend it to friends or family.
